prompt:
You describe a graph or chart from an electronics datasheet for an engineer who cannot see it.

Cover, in this order:
1. What is plotted against what: for each axis, the quantity, the unit and the range (first and last tick labels).
2. Each curve or series: its label or condition (temperature, voltage, mode, ...) and its overall trend in words.
3. Values printed in the figure as text (annotations, labelled points, legend values). Do not estimate values from where a curve sits; if a value is not printed, describe the trend in words instead.

Figure type: graph or chart
Section: 4 Electrical Specifications > 4.2 RF Receive Section > 868/915 MHz
Caption: Figure 7: Typical Selectivity at 500 kBaud Data Rate, 868 MHz, GFSK, IF Frequency is 355 kHz and the Digital Channel Filter Bandwidth is 812 kHz
Text inside the figure (exact, from the PDF text layer): -30 | -20 | -10 | 0 | 10 | 20 | 30 | 40 | 50 | 60 | -40 -30 -20 -10 0 10 20 30 40 | Offset [MHz] | Blocking [dB] | -20 | -10 | 0 | 10 | 20 | 30 | 40 | -2 -1,5 -1 -0,5 0 0,5 1 1,5 2 | Selectivity [dB]
Text that mentions the figure: Offset [MHz]

Rules:
- When a name or number from "Text inside the figure" is visible in the image, copy it exactly, character for character.
- Never invent a value, name, pin, unit or connection. If something is too small or blurry to read, write "unreadable" instead of guessing.
- Describe only what this image shows. Do not explain general theory or add advice.
- Mention each item once. Stop when everything is covered.
- Plain text only: no Markdown headings, tables or bold. Short paragraphs and "- " lists are fine.
- Start directly with what the figure is (for example "Block diagram of ..."), not with "The image shows".

answer.text:
Graph of Blocking vs Offset [MHz] and Selectivity vs Offset [MHz].

Left graph:
Y-axis: Blocking [dB], range from -30 to 60.
X-axis: Offset [MHz], range from -40 to 40.
Curve: One curve showing the typical blocking characteristic. The trend starts high around 50 dB at -40 MHz, decreases to a minimum near 0 dB around -10 MHz, then increases to about 45 dB at 40 MHz.
Text inside the figure: -30 | -20 | -10 | 0 | 10 | 20 | 30 | 40 | 50 | 60 | -40 -30 -20 -10 0 10 20 30 40 | Offset [MHz] | Blocking [dB]

Right graph:
Y-axis: Selectivity [dB], range from -20 to 40.
X-axis: Offset [MHz], range from -2 to 2.
Curve: One curve showing the typical selectivity characteristic. The trend starts around 35 dB at -2 MHz, decreases to a minimum around -15 dB near 0 MHz, and then increases to about 35 dB at 2 MHz.
Text inside the figure: -2 -1,5 -1 -0,5 0 0,5 1 1,5 2 | Selectivity [dB]

Caption: Figure 7: Typical Selectivity at 500 kBaud Data Rate, 868 MHz, GFSK, IF Frequency is 355 kHz and the Digital Channel Filter Bandwidth is 812 kHz.
Text that mentions the figure: Offset [MHz]
